context.prd-excerpt:
Feature: Tag links (slug: tag-links, should-have).
As someone collecting links, I want to tag what I save and filter by tag, so that a shelf of two hundred links stays usable.
Attach zero or more free-text tags to a link, and filter the list endpoint by tag.
Tags are a separate table with a many-to-many join to links, not a comma-separated string column. This is the one place the fixture deliberately requires a real relationship: a single-table shortcut would make the data-model layer trivial and the fixture would stop exercising the part of layer planning most likely to break.
Considerations (verbatim from the feature): Tag names are matched case-sensitively. Case folding is a reasonable product decision but it is not free to verify, and leaving it explicit here stops an implementer inventing either behaviour and calling it correct.
This feature is should-have rather than must-have so layer planning has to decide where a lower-priority item lands, rather than treating every feature identically.
CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS TASK: - A real join table is REQUIRED. Do not replace it with a comma-separated string column on `links`, a JSON array column, or a SQLAlchemy `ARRAY`. The feature rules the shortcut out by name. - The `Tag` half of the data model above was declared by L1-002 and already exists. This task declares the `LinkTag` half and wires the two entities together. - Nothing here folds case. This task adds no lookup by name, but if the implementer writes one for a test it must use `Tag.name == value`, never `lower()` or `ilike`.
OPEN GAP, DELIBERATELY NOT RESOLVED HERE (tag-links gap 1, kind=decision, raised 2026-08-27): "Whether a tag with no remaining links is deleted or kept is undecided. Keeping them makes an autocomplete list easy and lets the list rot." Do NOT implement any orphan-tag cleanup: no `cascade="all, delete-orphan"` reaching Tag, no `ON DELETE` clause intended to remove tags, no post-delete hook. Inventing a policy for an undecided question is out of scope for this task and for L2-003.
context.tech-stack: Python 3.11 SQLAlchemy 2.x - use the 2.0 typed declarative style: `Mapped[...]` annotations with `mapped_column(...)`, and `relationship(...)` for the association. Do NOT use the legacy `Column(...)` form and do NOT use `declarative_base()`. SQLite, file-backed (database, no external server). IMPORTANT SQLite behaviour: foreign key constraints are DECLARED in the DDL but are NOT ENFORCED unless `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` is issued per connection, and L0-003's engine does not issue it. So a `LinkTag` row pointing at a non-existent link id will insert without error. Do not write a test asserting that an orphan foreign key raises, and do not add the pragma - L2-003 checks that a link exists in Python and returns 404 (tag-links criterion 4). The composite PRIMARY KEY, by contrast, IS enforced by SQLite, and this task tests it. pytest 8.x (test runner), run as `python -m pytest` from the repository root FastAPI 0.110+ and httpx are installed but are NOT used by this task - a model has no HTTP surface. All distributions are already installed by L0-001.

task.objective:
Declare the `LinkTag` join table - one row per attachment of one tag to one link, with a composite primary key over (link_id, tag_id) - and add the many-to-many `tags` attribute to the existing `Link` model so a link can be read and written with its tags.
This task builds the storage that the Layer 2 endpoints satisfy their acceptance criteria through. It satisfies none of tag-links' criteria itself: those are HTTP-level (200, 404, filtered listings) and are met by L2-003 and L2-002 through this table. What this task guarantees is the storage-level property those endpoints lean on - the composite primary key makes a second attachment of the same tag to the same link impossible, which is what makes re-tagging idempotent underneath tag-links criterion 2.
This task defines no route, no Pydantic schema, and no orphan-tag cleanup policy.

requirements.requirement:
Create `app/models/link_tag.py` with exactly this content:
"""The LinkTag join table: the many-to-many association between links and tags."""
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey, Integer from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from app.database import Base
class LinkTag(Base): """One attachment of one tag to one link. The primary key is the pair."""
__tablename__ = "link_tags"
link_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column( Integer, ForeignKey("links.id"), primary_key=True ) tag_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column( Integer, ForeignKey("tags.id"), primary_key=True )
Decisions embedded above that must be preserved exactly as written:
- `__tablename__ = "link_tags"`. Lower-case plural, matching `links` and `tags`.
- BOTH columns carry `primary_key=True`. Together they form ONE composite primary key over (link_id, tag_id) - not two separate keys, and not a surrogate `id` column with a separate unique constraint. This is the whole point of the table: SQLite rejects a second row with the same pair, so attaching a tag a link already carries cannot create a duplicate row. Do NOT add an `id` column.
- `ForeignKey("links.id")` and `ForeignKey("tags.id")` are written as strings naming the tables L1-001 and L1-002 created. Do not import `Link` or `Tag` into this module; the string form is resolved from `Base.metadata` and keeps this module free of imports that would complicate the import order in `app/models/__init__.py`.
- No `ondelete=` clause and no `cascade`. Orphan-tag policy is the feature's open gap 1 and is deliberately undecided; adding a delete rule here would answer it by accident.
- No extra column. The join carries no `created_at`, no `position`, no `id`. The feature declares two columns and this table has two columns.

MODIFY `app/models/link.py`. It already exists, created by L1-001, and currently contains exactly this:
"""The Link model: one stored URL with an optional title."""
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from sqlalchemy import DateTime, Integer, Text from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from app.database import Base
def utcnow() -> datetime: """Return the current UTC time as a naive datetime, to microsecond resolution.""" return datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
class Link(Base): """A saved link: a URL, an optional title, and when it was stored."""
__tablename__ = "links"
id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True) url: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=False) title: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True) created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column( DateTime, nullable=False, default=utcnow )
Rewrite it to exactly this - three added imports and one added attribute, everything else byte-for-byte unchanged:
"""The Link model: one stored URL with an optional title, plus its tags."""
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from sqlalchemy import DateTime, Integer, Text from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship
from app.database import Base from app.models.link_tag import LinkTag from app.models.tag import Tag
def utcnow() -> datetime: """Return the current UTC time as a naive datetime, to microsecond resolution.""" return datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
class Link(Base): """A saved link: a URL, an optional title, when it was stored, and its tags."""
__tablename__ = "links"
id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True) url: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=False) title: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True) created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column( DateTime, nullable=False, default=utcnow )
tags: Mapped[list[Tag]] = relationship( Tag, secondary=LinkTag.__table__, lazy="selectin", order_by=Tag.id, )
Decisions embedded above that must be preserved exactly as written:
- The four existing columns, the `utcnow` function and `__tablename__` are UNCHANGED. `tests/test_model_link.py` from L1-001 still runs and still asserts all of them, including that `url` is not unique. Changing any of them breaks a passing test.
- `secondary=LinkTag.__table__` uses the join table declared in requirement 1. The import `from app.models.link_tag import LinkTag` is a real runtime import, not a string reference, so the association is resolved eagerly and cannot fail later with an unresolved-name error. There is no import cycle: `link_tag.py` imports only `app.database`, and `tag.py` imports only `app.database`. Neither imports `link.py`.
- This is a ONE-WAY relationship. There is no `back_populates` and no `backref`, and `app/models/tag.py` is NOT edited. `Tag` therefore has no `.links` attribute, by design - nothing downstream needs one. L2-002 filters from the tag side with an explicit join: select(Link).join(LinkTag, LinkTag.link_id == Link.id) .join(Tag, Tag.id == LinkTag.tag_id) .where(Tag.name == tag)
- `lazy="selectin"` loads every link's tags in one extra SELECT when a set of links is queried, instead of one SELECT per link. L2-002 returns a whole list of links with their tags, so the default `lazy="select"` would issue N+1 queries there.
- `order_by=Tag.id` makes `link.tags` come back in a stable order - tag id ascending, which is the order the tags were first created. The feature states no ordering for tags, and an unordered collection would make a response body assertion in L2-003 flaky, so a deterministic order is chosen here and recorded as a decision rather than left to the database.
- No `cascade` argument. The default for a `secondary` relationship removes only the association rows, never a `Tag` row. Orphan-tag policy is the feature's open gap 1 and stays unanswered.

MODIFY `app/models/__init__.py`. It already imports `Link` and `Tag` (added by L1-001 and L1-002). Rewrite it to exactly this:
"""SQLAlchemy models for Link Shelf."""
from app.models.link import Link from app.models.link_tag import LinkTag from app.models.tag import Tag
__all__ = ["Link", "LinkTag", "Tag"]
All three names must be present. `tests/conftest.py` runs `import app.models` before calling `Base.metadata.create_all`, so a model that is not imported here has no table and every test touching it fails with "no such table: link_tags".
Import order note: `from app.models.link import Link` runs first and `link.py` itself imports `app.models.link_tag` and `app.models.tag`. That is safe - Python already has the partially-initialised `app.models` package in `sys.modules` and loads the two submodules directly - and neither submodule imports `link.py` back. Do not reorder these three lines to try to "fix" an import cycle; there is none.

Do NOT create or edit any other file. Specifically: do not touch `app/models/tag.py`, `app/database.py`, `app/main.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_setup.py`, `tests/test_model_link.py`, `tests/test_model_tag.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt` or `.gitignore`. Do not create a Pydantic schema, a router, a route or a migration - this project has no migration tool, the schema is created from `Base.metadata`. Do not add `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`. Do not run `git init` and do not touch `.git`.

exports.interface:
# app/models/link_tag.py from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey, Integer from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from app.database import Base
class LinkTag(Base): __tablename__ = "link_tags"
link_id: Mapped[int] # Integer, FK -> links.id, part of the composite primary key tag_id: Mapped[int] # Integer, FK -> tags.id, part of the composite primary key
Import as: `from app.models import LinkTag` (also `from app.models.link_tag import LinkTag`)
Downstream contract: - The primary key is the PAIR (link_id, tag_id). A second row with the same pair raises `sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError`. Re-attaching a tag a link already carries is therefore impossible at the storage layer; L2-003 must check membership before appending (e.g. `if tag not in link.tags: link.tags.append(tag)`) rather than relying on the exception. - There is no `id` column and no extra column. - Foreign keys are declared but NOT enforced by SQLite at runtime (no `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`). A row pointing at a missing link id inserts silently, so L2-003 must look the link up in Python and return 404 when it is absent - the database will not do it. - No delete rule is declared. Whether a tag with no remaining links is deleted or kept is the tag-links open gap 1 and is still undecided; nothing here answers it.

Downstream contract: - `link.tags` is a `list[Tag]`, empty (never None) when nothing is attached. - Attach with `link.tags.append(tag)` then `db.commit()`; that writes one `link_tags` row. Detach with `link.tags.remove(tag)`, which deletes the association row and leaves the `Tag` row alone. - The order is `Tag.id` ascending - stable across reloads, so a response body listing tags may be asserted directly without sorting. - `lazy="selectin"` means listing N links loads their tags in ONE additional query, not N. - The relationship is ONE-WAY. `Tag` has no `.links` attribute. To go from a tag name to its links, join explicitly: select(Link) .join(LinkTag, LinkTag.link_id == Link.id) .join(Tag, Tag.id == LinkTag.tag_id) .where(Tag.name == tag_name) `Tag.name == tag_name` is a case-sensitive comparison and must stay one - never `func.lower()` or `ilike`. - Link's four columns are unchanged: `url` is still not unique, `title` is still nullable, `created_at` is still naive UTC with microsecond resolution and still orders newest-first via `Link.created_at.desc()`.
